title: Deferred rollback horizon and telemetry-driven safepoint coordinator
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: We deploy config changes (batching policy, cache TTLs, kernel selection heuristics) that can cause large, non-linear cost regressions or sudden latency regressions due to KV cache invalidation or batch shape changes. Existing rollback mechanisms trigger immediately on error-rate bursts, but that leads to unnecessary thrashing for transient signals and doesn't account for cost telemetry or the stateful nature of KV caches and batching queues.

Proposal: Implement a "deferred rollback horizon" + "safepoint coordinator" that: (1) creates lightweight safepoints before risky config applies, (2) observes multi-dimensional telemetry (latency P95/P99, error rate, per-model token cost, KV cache miss rate, batch-size distribution), (3) waits a tunable horizon before irreversible rollback, and (4) performs staged, state-aware rollbacks including KV quarantine and batch drains to avoid cache storms. The coordinator will synthesize a single safety score from telemetry and cost signals and expose human-readable justification in the console for post-mortem and manual approvals.

Key differences vs. existing approaches: focuses on deferred windows (horizon), cost-aware decisions (token spend & burst cost), and explicit state reconciliation steps (KV quarantine, staged cache warming, batch draining) rather than immediate global revert. This should reduce false positive rollbacks, reduce cost spikes from cache rebuilds, and allow safe partial rollbacks targeted at the layer (routing vs kernel) that caused regression.
acceptance_criteria: When a config apply is initiated, a safepoint object is recorded and visible in Console with links to the apply and baseline telemetry snapshot.
Coordinator computes a safety score within 30s and updates it every minute during the horizon window.
Automated rollback only triggers after safety score crosses critical threshold for at least two consecutive evaluation windows (configurable), or immediately if an emergency/error trigger fires.
Rollback sequence performs KV quarantine before unrolling config, drains in-flight batches, and warms caches to target hit-rate >= 60% before removing quarantine (simulated in staging).
End-to-end integration tests (staging) demonstrate reduction in unnecessary rollbacks and a decrease in post-rollback token cost spikes compared to the current immediate-revert baseline.
Console shows cost delta attribution (tokens/day) and a short rationale for each automatic rollback event for the last 90 days.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): implement coordinator + safepoint proto and basic telemetry ingest. Feature flagged behind 'deferred_rollback'.
Phase 1 (staging): run coordinator in observe-only mode for 2 weeks on our staging fleet and synth workloads that cause KV churn and batch shape shifts.
Phase 2 (canary): enable automated decisions on 5% of production hosts with conservative horizon=15m and threshold tuning; human-approval fallback on critical customers.
Phase 3 (ramp): expand to 50% with progressive relaxation of the horizon to default 5m once thresholds are validated; enable partial layer rollbacks (routing/kernel) for supported models.
Phase 4 (global): flip default to enable deferred rollback for all applies, with policy opt-outs per-customer (Dedicated/Private).
test_plan: Unit tests for safepoint lifecycle, safety-score calculations, and config state machine transitions.

Integration test: simulate a batch policy misconfiguration that increases per-token cost by 2x; verify coordinator delays rollback and then performs KV quarantine + staged rollback with controlled cache warm-up.
Chaos test: inject intermittent latency spikes and transient error bursts to validate horizon prevents thrash.
Load test: measure coordinator CPU/memory overhead at 10k concurrent safepoints per minute (target < 200ms per evaluation cycle).
Post-rollback validation: automatic run of standard eval prompt set to ensure output quality hasn't regressed after rollback.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: deferred_rollback.safepoints.created.count -> alert on sudden increase (indicates mass applies).
Metric: deferred_rollback.safety_score.histogram -> alert if median goes below safe threshold for > 30m.
Metric: kv_quarantine.hit_rate -> alert if quarantine prevents cache rebuild for > 60m.
Dashboard: per-apply timeline (safepoint creation, safety score, trigger reason, cost delta, rollback action).
Incident runbook: steps for manual abort of an automated rollback; how to pin model version and perform safe cache reseed.
comments: 2025-02-18 Marco Chen: Created ticket. Initial scope includes safepoints, safety-score calc, KV quarantine, and staged rollback orchestration. Linking to config-apply PR template doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Config+Apply+Checklist

2025-02-20 Priya Desai: Spike notes - implemented prototype safety-score that weights latency P99 (0.5), token cost delta (0.3), and KV miss delta (0.2). Observed noisy score during short-lived GC events; added exponential smoothing in latest branch. See draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4129

2025-02-24 SRE review (Ana Lopez): Concern about KV quarantine causing prolonged cold-cache penalties for SLO-sensitive customers. Recommendation: customer opt-out and aggressive cache warmup path. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-27 PM feedback (Javier Ortega): Add console rationale and cost attribution so product can review automated events before opening support cases. Also requested a manual 'force-reconcile' button in Console for on-call.

2025-03-01 Engineering review: Decided to implement two rollback modes: 'staged' (default) and 'immediate' (emergency). Staged includes three-phase safepoint unwind: quiesce, config unapply, cache-warm. Immediate bypasses quarantine and restores last known-good state (only for critical errors).

2025-03-02 Priya Desai: Implemented safepoint proto and telemetry ingestion; hooked safety_score into the apply state machine (observe-only). Beginning stash tests in staging cluster. Next: simulate cost regressions and tune thresholds.
